# Database options

30 options. Set them in the daemon's `.conf` file or `appsettings.json`. Full reference: [configuration.md](../configuration.md). All areas: [index](README.md).

Daemon says which server reads it. Reload says whether `.reload config` applies it: `live` is applied to the running server, `restart` keeps its value until the next start, `start` is read once when the daemon starts.

## `Database`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Auth:ConnectionString` | `string` | `""` | text | Both, Gateway | start | The connection string of this component's database. The shipped files carry the development placeholder user `arcane`; change it for any real deployment. |
| `Auth:Provider` | `DatabaseProvider` | `MariaDb` | MariaDb \| MySql \| PostgreSql \| Sqlite | Both, Gateway | start | The relational engine of this component's database (`Database:Auth`, `Database:Characters` or `Database:World`). Values: `MariaDb`, `MySql`, `PostgreSql`, `Sqlite`. |
| `Auth:SqliteBusyTimeoutMs` | `int?` | `null` | a whole number from 0 to 60000 | Both, Gateway | start | SQLite only: this component's busy timeout in milliseconds (0..60000), overriding `Database:SqliteBusyTimeoutMs`. Unset inherits it. Other engines ignore it. |
| `Auth:SqliteSynchronous` | `SqliteSynchronousMode?` | `null` | Full \| Normal | Both, Gateway | start | SQLite only: this component's `PRAGMA synchronous` (Full or Normal), overriding `Database:SqliteSynchronous`. Unset inherits it. Normal avoids the fsync stall at every commit but can lose the most recent commits on power loss or an OS crash; it is applied only when the database is in WAL mode, otherwise the database stays on Full and an error is logged. Other engines ignore it. Values: `Full`, `Normal`. |
| `Auth:WriterLockDatabase` | `string` | `null` | text | Both, Gateway | start | PostgreSQL only: the existing maintenance database the single-writer advisory lock is taken in (overrides `Database:WriterLockDatabase`; unset inherits it, default `postgres`). PostgreSQL scopes advisory locks to the database a session is connected to, so every world must take the lock in the same database, and it must exist before the characters database does. The login needs CONNECT on it. Only the characters database takes the single-writer lock, so this key has an effect under `Database:Characters` only and the realm daemon ignores it; under `Database:Auth` and `Database:World` it does nothing. MariaDB, MySQL and SQLite ignore it. |
| `Characters:ConnectionString` | `string` | `""` | text | World, Gateway | start | The connection string of this component's database. The shipped files carry the development placeholder user `arcane`; change it for any real deployment. |
| `Characters:Provider` | `DatabaseProvider` | `MariaDb` | MariaDb \| MySql \| PostgreSql \| Sqlite | World, Gateway | start | The relational engine of this component's database (`Database:Auth`, `Database:Characters` or `Database:World`). Values: `MariaDb`, `MySql`, `PostgreSql`, `Sqlite`. |
| `Characters:SqliteBusyTimeoutMs` | `int?` | `null` | a whole number from 0 to 60000 | World, Gateway | start | SQLite only: this component's busy timeout in milliseconds (0..60000), overriding `Database:SqliteBusyTimeoutMs`. Unset inherits it. Other engines ignore it. |
| `Characters:SqliteSynchronous` | `SqliteSynchronousMode?` | `null` | Full \| Normal | World, Gateway | start | SQLite only: this component's `PRAGMA synchronous` (Full or Normal), overriding `Database:SqliteSynchronous`. Unset inherits it. Normal avoids the fsync stall at every commit but can lose the most recent commits on power loss or an OS crash; it is applied only when the database is in WAL mode, otherwise the database stays on Full and an error is logged. Other engines ignore it. Values: `Full`, `Normal`. |
| `Characters:WriterLockDatabase` | `string` | `null` | text | World, Gateway | start | PostgreSQL only: the existing maintenance database the single-writer advisory lock is taken in (overrides `Database:WriterLockDatabase`; unset inherits it, default `postgres`). PostgreSQL scopes advisory locks to the database a session is connected to, so every world must take the lock in the same database, and it must exist before the characters database does. The login needs CONNECT on it. Only the characters database takes the single-writer lock, so this key has an effect under `Database:Characters` only and the realm daemon ignores it; under `Database:Auth` and `Database:World` it does nothing. MariaDB, MySQL and SQLite ignore it. |
| `ConnectionString` | `string` | `""` | text | Both, Gateway | start | The connection string for any component that has no `Database:<Component>` sub-section of its own. The shipped Realm file uses this single-database form. |
| `Provider` | `DatabaseProvider` | `MariaDb` | MariaDb \| MySql \| PostgreSql \| Sqlite | Both, Gateway | start | The relational engine for any component that has no `Database:<Component>` sub-section of its own (the single-database layout). MariaDB is the primary engine; MySql, PostgreSql and Sqlite are also supported. Values: `MariaDb`, `MySql`, `PostgreSql`, `Sqlite`. |
| `SlowCommandWarnMs` | `int` | `2000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | Both, Gateway | start | How long (milliseconds, default 2000; 0 disables) a single database command may take to execute before it is logged at WARN with the DbContext, whether it ran inside a transaction or autocommitted, whether it was a write, the first 80 characters of its SQL (parameter values are never logged) and the code that issued it, on every provider. It sees what the transaction warning cannot: writes that autocommit and wait in "database is locked". Identical warnings are limited to one per 10 s (docs/areas/persistence.md). |
| `SlowTransactionWarnMs` | `int` | `2000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | Both, Gateway | start | How long (milliseconds, default 2000; 0 disables) a database transaction may stay open before it is logged at WARN with the DbContext and the code that closed it, on every provider. A transaction that holds the write lock this long is what makes other writers fail with "database is locked", so the next holder names itself in the log (docs/areas/persistence.md). |
| `Sqlite:Checkpoint:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | true \| false | Both, Gateway | start | Whether the background checkpointer owns checkpointing (default true). False leaves SQLite's own auto-checkpoint (1000 pages, inside the committing connection) untouched. |
| `Sqlite:Checkpoint:IntervalMs` | `int` | `2000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | Both, Gateway | start | How often (milliseconds, 100..3600000, default 2000) the background service runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)` on each database. PASSIVE takes no writer lock and waits on no lock, but its I/O still competes for the same disk; a shorter interval keeps the WAL smaller at the cost of more wake-ups. |
| `Sqlite:Checkpoint:JournalSizeLimitBytes` | `long` | `33554432` | a whole number from 0 to 1099511627776 | Both, Gateway | start | `PRAGMA journal_size_limit` in bytes (0..1099511627776, default 33554432 = 32 MiB), set on every connection to the database: once a checkpoint has copied the whole WAL into the database and the next writer restarts it, SQLite truncates the file down to this size instead of leaving it at its high-water mark. This is the only thing that shrinks the -wal file while the server runs, and only when the log restarts (continuous overlapping readers can postpone that; a warning is logged when the file stays above 4 x max(this limit, 1 MiB) for 30 s while commits keep arriving or the copy is incomplete): the service never runs a TRUNCATE checkpoint during operation, because TRUNCATE takes the exclusive writer lock and holds it through the copy of the frames written since the last PASSIVE, the WAL fsync and the database fsync (which on Windows flushes every page earlier PASSIVE runs wrote), which would put the stall this feature removes back in front of a game save. Only the final checkpoint at host stop, after the world has drained its saves, is a TRUNCATE; it waits at most about 250 ms for readers and writers, and holds the writer lock through its copy and syncs. If the Auth database is one file shared by the world and realm daemons, either daemon's shutdown TRUNCATE can briefly stall the other's auth writes. |
| `Sqlite:SingleWriter:StatsIntervalMs` | `int` | `300000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | Both, Gateway | start | How often (milliseconds, 0..3600000, default 300000; 0 never) each gate logs one INFO line with its writes, contended writes, waits, longest hold and timeouts for the interval. |
| `SqliteBusyTimeoutMs` | `int` | `5000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | Both, Gateway | start | SQLite only: how long (0..60000 ms, default 5000) a connection waits inside SQLite for another connection's write lock before reporting "database is locked", set as `PRAGMA busy_timeout` on every connection (never more than the connection string's Default Timeout, and clamped to `Resilience:Database:QueryTimeoutMs` when the database guard is on, so a refused call never outlives its deadline in SQLite's busy handler). Without it a waiting writer retries only every 150 ms, so the many background writers on one SQLite file starve each other. 0 disables the pragma. MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL ignore it (docs/areas/persistence.md). |
| `SqliteSynchronous` | `SqliteSynchronousMode` | `Full` | Full \| Normal | Both, Gateway | start | SQLite only: the `PRAGMA synchronous` set on every connection, Full (default) or Normal. Full fsyncs the WAL at every commit, so a committed save survives power loss. Normal skips that fsync, which removes multi-second commit stalls on a slow disk (and the "database is locked" failures they cause in other writers); the database stays consistent, but the most recent commits can be lost on power loss or an OS crash, never on an application crash. Normal is applied only to a database that is in WAL mode (the schema bootstrap switches file databases to WAL, best effort): a database that is not in WAL mode (the switch failed or was refused) stays on Full and an error is logged, because Normal outside WAL can corrupt the database on power loss. Each component may override it with a Database:Auth, Database:Characters or Database:World SqliteSynchronous key. MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL ignore it (docs/areas/persistence.md). Values: `Full`, `Normal`. |
| `SqliteWriteTimeoutMs` | `int` | `5000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | Both, Gateway | start | SQLite only, characters database only: the longest (0..60000 ms, default 5000; rounded up to whole seconds) any command on a characters connection waits for another connection's write lock before it fails as "database is locked". It is written into the connection string's Default Timeout (30 s) when smaller, and replaces 0 (unlimited), so it bounds every command including EF's first one and its `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and through the busy-timeout clamp SQLite's own wait. Without it a writer holding the file for a minute held each save queue's single consumer for the full 30 s per attempt. Failed saves are retained and retried by their queues. 0 keeps the connection string's Default Timeout. MariaDB, MySQL and PostgreSQL ignore it (docs/areas/persistence.md). |
| `Upgrade:LockTimeoutSeconds` | `int` | `60` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | Both, Gateway | start | How long a start waits for another process's schema work, in seconds; must be 1..86400 or the start is refused as a configuration error. |
| `Upgrade:Policy` | `SchemaPolicy` | `Always` | Always \| CreateOnly \| Never | Both, Gateway | start | What a start may do to the schema. `Always` (default) creates and upgrades; `CreateOnly` creates an empty database but refuses to upgrade an existing one (the retail-like setting for production, where `arcane-db upgrade` applies updates); `Never` only verifies. See docs/ops/database-upgrade.md. Values: `Always`, `CreateOnly`, `Never`. |
| `Upgrade:ValidateOnly` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | Both, Gateway | start | When true, serving nodes run startup schema checks in validate-only mode: zero DDL and zero seed inserts are executed, and startup fails closed if any component schema is missing, behind, or ahead of the build's current version. Default is `false`. See docs/ops/database-upgrade.md. |

| `World:Provider` | `DatabaseProvider` | `MariaDb` | MariaDb \| MySql \| PostgreSql \| Sqlite | World | start | The relational engine of this component's database (`Database:Auth`, `Database:Characters` or `Database:World`). Values: `MariaDb`, `MySql`, `PostgreSql`, `Sqlite`. |
| `World:SqliteBusyTimeoutMs` | `int?` | `null` | a whole number from 0 to 60000 | World | start | SQLite only: this component's busy timeout in milliseconds (0..60000), overriding `Database:SqliteBusyTimeoutMs`. Unset inherits it. Other engines ignore it. |
| `World:SqliteSynchronous` | `SqliteSynchronousMode?` | `null` | Full \| Normal | World | start | SQLite only: this component's `PRAGMA synchronous` (Full or Normal), overriding `Database:SqliteSynchronous`. Unset inherits it. Normal avoids the fsync stall at every commit but can lose the most recent commits on power loss or an OS crash; it is applied only when the database is in WAL mode, otherwise the database stays on Full and an error is logged. Other engines ignore it. Values: `Full`, `Normal`. |
| `World:WriterLockDatabase` | `string` | `null` | text | World | start | PostgreSQL only: the existing maintenance database the single-writer advisory lock is taken in (overrides `Database:WriterLockDatabase`; unset inherits it, default `postgres`). PostgreSQL scopes advisory locks to the database a session is connected to, so every world must take the lock in the same database, and it must exist before the characters database does. The login needs CONNECT on it. Only the characters database takes the single-writer lock, so this key has an effect under `Database:Characters` only and the realm daemon ignores it; under `Database:Auth` and `Database:World` it does nothing. MariaDB, MySQL and SQLite ignore it. |
| `WriterLockDatabase` | `string` | `"postgres"` | text | Both, Gateway | start | PostgreSQL only: the existing maintenance database (default `postgres`) in which the world takes its single-writer advisory lock. PostgreSQL scopes advisory locks to the database the session is connected to, so all worlds of one characters database must lock in the same database, one that exists before the characters database is created. The login needs CONNECT on it. Only the characters database takes the single-writer lock, so the world uses this value (or the Database:Characters WriterLockDatabase key that overrides it) for the characters database alone; the realm daemon and the Auth and World components ignore it. MariaDB, MySQL and SQLite ignore it (docs/guide/operations.md). |
